title: Returned it
body: The warm-water back-inflate buoyancy compensator lasted 44 dives before I gave up on it. The night dive was the highlight, with octopus and a sleeping turtle under a ledge. Fits tight across the shoulders and baggy at the waist. The water temperature changed a lot between sites, from bathtub warm to properly cold at depth. Runs small, order a size up. Conditions varied from flat calm to a strong surge on the outer wall. Passed its EN250 bench test after a year without any adjustment. I rinsed everything in fresh water after each day and let it dry in the shade. The shop service was straightforward and parts were in stock. I have been diving for about eight years, mostly in the Pacific Northwest. Holds me flat in the water and I never feel pushed face down. I compared it side by side with the older model my buddy uses. Very stable and I trim out horizontal without effort. Packing up at the end of the trip gave me a chance to look it over closely for wear. The release handles are hard to find with gloves on. Back home I used it again for a cold quarry dive to see how it compared. Weight pockets slipped out of their slots on the entry. We also did a deeper dive to about thirty metres on a wreck that sits on sand. The inflator button stuck and kept filling the bladder on ascent. On the second day we had a long drift along the reef with a lot of current at the start. Dumps are slow, I struggled to control my ascent. Feels cheap and flimsy. Something broke within the first month.

Deco planning felt too aggressive for my liking on repetitive days. It resets my gas mix to air after every dive which is annoying. Setting the oxygen percentage is buried deep in the menus. title: Okay for the price
body: Mixed experience with this one at Les Escoumins. Packing up at the end of the trip gave me a chance to look it over closely for wear. No rust after a season in salt water with a quick rinse. The liveaboard crew were great and the briefings were thorough. Still shiny with no corrosion after months on the boat. On the second day we had a long drift along the reef with a lot of current at the start. Too small to be seen in any kind of chop. Visibility was poor on a couple of dives because of a plankton bloom. The colour fades into the waves, the boat took ages to find us. Conditions varied from flat calm to a strong surge on the outer wall. Deploys cleanly from mid-water with a single breath. My buddy and I are both advanced open water divers with a couple of hundred logged dives between us. Shooting it from the safety stop is easy and it stands upright. We also did a deeper dive to about thirty metres on a wreck that sits on sand. Arrived two days after ordering and was packed well. The dive centre staff were curious about it and a few of them asked to try it. Customer service answered my sizing question quickly. I have been diving for about eight years, mostly in the Pacific Northwest. The night dive was the highlight, with octopus and a sleeping turtle under a ledge.
